summary: In an unprecedented acknowledgment, the U.S. Space Force confirmed it has deployed operational weapons in orbit to serve as a deterrent, as military leadership warned that defense domains now extend to cislunar space. On the acquisitions front, Northrop Grumman was named prime contractor for the Space Force’s Ground Moving Target Indicator program. In civil space and science, NASA powered on instruments aboard the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and extended its planned mission to 22 years following a successful engine burn. Meanwhile, NASA’s lunar orbiter detected a rare "once-in-century" impact crater on the Moon, astronomers discovered the youngest known planet, and satellite tracking confirmed that seasonal movement of water and ice shifts Earth’s center of mass annually. Operationally, NASA fully restored its Guam ground station following damage from Typhoon Mawar, the Curiosity rover marked 5,000 days on Mars, and an inspector general report warned of persistent cybersecurity deficiencies across NASA networks. In commercial and international developments, Russia launched its Progress 96 cargo craft to the International Space Station, Viasat and Space42 committed up to $1 billion to their Equatys joint venture, SEOPS booked five launches on Isar Aerospace's Spectrum rocket, and SpaceX’s Falcon 9 landing team received the inaugural Neil Armstrong Space Prize. Looking ahead, industry observers should watch as SpaceX prepares for the first orbital test flight of its Starship rocket.
